77: Yudan the Distinguished - Yudan was his name, and he was a great one of his generation. Anywhere the appellation Biribi is used it has the meaning of wisdom and sharpness.
Only the earlobe - the lobe of the ear, in the flesh and not on the ridge.

And the Rabbis say, etc. - they disagree with [Yudan]. This is their proof: it is established for us that a Hebrew slave who is a priest is not pierced, because this would make him blemished, and he will no longer be able to return to his original status. Later on, we derive from "And he shall return to his own family” (Leviticus 25:41) -- to his status in his family (Kiddushin 21b:12). How then can he be rendered blemished? Did we not learn in a Mishna, regarding blemishes, "[the firstborn is considered blemished, and may be slaughtered outside the Temple] if the ear was damaged from the cartilage but not if the skin was damaged" (Bekhorot 37a:15).
He is pierced only, etc. - you may learn from here that we only pierce on the upper part of the ear.
With regard to what do they disagree - regarding a sharp thorn and a thorn.
